questions.question: Explain the aetiology and symptoms of upper gastrointestinal tract disorders.
questions.solution_html:
• Aetiology (Causes) – 2–(3 marks)
  • ● Infection (e.g., H. pylori in gastritis/ulcer) – (1 mark)
  • ● Dietary factors – spicy foods, alcohol, irregular meals – (1 mark)
  • ● Stress and lifestyle factors (smoking, poor eating habits) – ½–(1 mark)
  • ● Drug use (NSAIDs, steroids) – ½–(1 mark)
  • ● Excess acid secretion / reflux (e.g., Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease) – ½–(1 mark)
  • Symptoms – 2–(3 marks)
  • ● Epigastric pain or burning sensation – (1 mark)
  • ● Nausea and vomiting – (1 mark)
  • ● Heartburn and acid regurgitation – (1 mark)
  • ● Loss of appetite, bloating, indigestion – ½–(1 mark)
  • ● In severe cases: bleeding, weight loss – ½–(1 mark)
questions.final_answer: ● In severe cases: bleeding, weight loss – ½
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe plant-source food allergens.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Definition: Plant-source food allergens are allergenic substances present in foods derived
  • from plants that can trigger immune reactions in sensitive individuals – (1 mark)
  • ● Common sources
  • Peanuts, Soybeans, Wheat, tree nuts (e.g., Almonds) – (1 mark)
  • ● Allergenic components
  • Proteins such as storage proteins, gluten (in wheat), and other plant proteins – (1 mark)
  • ● Symptoms caused
  • Skin reactions (rash, itching), gastrointestinal issues, respiratory problems, and in severe
  • cases anaphylaxis – (1 mark)
  • ● Management
  • Avoidance of allergenic foods, proper food labeling awareness, substitution with
  • hypoallergenic alternatives – (1 mark)
questions.final_answer: hypoallergenic alternatives
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain macronutrient deficiencies in AIDS.
questions.solution_html:
• ● Definition/Overview
  • In Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome, macronutrient deficiencies occur due to
  • increased metabolic demands, poor intake, and malabsorption – (1 mark)
  • ● Causes
  • Reduced appetite, infections, malabsorption, drug side effects, and increased
  • energy/protein needs – (1 mark)
  • ● Protein deficiency
  • Leads to muscle wasting, weight loss, weakened immunity (cachexia) – (1 mark)
  • ● Energy (carbohydrate & fat) deficiency
  • Causes fatigue, severe weight loss, and loss of body fat stores – (1 mark)
  • ● Consequences/Management
  • Leads to wasting syndrome; managed by high-calorie, high-protein diet, nutritional
  • support, and treatment of infections – (1 mark)
questions.final_answer: support, and treatment of infections
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the dietary guidelines for managing gastritis.
questions.solution_html:
• Dietary guidelines for managing gastritis
  • ● Eat small, frequent meals – avoids excess gastric acid secretion and reduces stomach
  • irritation ((1 mark))
  • ● Avoid irritant foods – such as spicy, fried, oily, and highly seasoned foods, which
  • increase gastric inflammation ((1 mark))
  • ● Limit gastric acid stimulants – avoid caffeine, alcohol, and carbonated beverages (1
  • mark)
  • ● Include bland, easily digestible foods – such as boiled rice, soft cereals, curd, and
  • well-cooked vegetables ((1 mark))
  • ● Maintain healthy eating habits & lifestyle – regular meal timing, avoid skipping meals
  • reduce stress, and avoid smoking ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: reduce stress, and avoid smoking ()
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the complications of AIDS. / Part D Essay
questions.solution_html:
• Complications of Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
  • ● Opportunistic infections – due to weakened immunity (e.g., tuberculosis, pneumonia
  • fungal infections) – (1 mark)
  • ● Cancers – increased risk of malignancies such as Kaposi’s sarcoma and lymphoma – 1
  • mark
  • ● Severe weight loss (wasting syndrome) – progressive loss of body weight and muscle
  • mass – (1 mark)
  • ● Neurological complications – memory loss, confusion, neuropathy, and dementia – 1
  • mark
  • ● Organ failure / multi-system involvement – chronic damage to lungs, liver, and other
  • organs leading to death if untreated – (1 mark)
  • Essay
questions.final_answer: Essay
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain lower gastrointestinal tract disorders with causes and symptoms.
questions.solution_html:
• A. Definition ((1 mark))
  • ● Disorders affecting the lower gastrointestinal tract (small intestine, large intestine
  • rectum, anus) that interfere with digestion, absorption, and elimination – ((1 mark))
  • B. Causes ((4 marks))
  • ● Infections (bacterial, viral, parasitic infections from contaminated food/water) – ((1 mark))
  • ● Dietary factors (low fiber diet, excessive junk food, irregular eating habits) – ((1 mark))
  • ● Inflammatory and functional disorders such as Inflammatory bowel disease and irritable
  • bowel conditions – ((1 mark))
  • ● Other factors: stress, medications, and altered gut flora – ((1 mark))
  • C. Symptoms ((4 marks))
  • ● Altered bowel habits: diarrhea or constipation – ((1 mark))
  • ● Abdominal pain and cramping – ((1 mark))
  • ● Bloating and flatulence – ((1 mark))
  • ● Severe signs: blood in stool, weight loss, dehydration, weakness – ((1 mark))
  • D. Conclusion ((1 mark))
  • ● Early diagnosis, dietary modification, and treatment of underlying cause are essential to
  • prevent complications – ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Option Definition ((1 mark))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain biochemical and immune tests used in food allergy diagnosis.
questions.solution_html:
• Biochemical and immune tests used in food allergy diagnosis
  • A. Biochemical tests ((5 marks))
  • ● Serum histamine level test – Measures histamine released during allergic reaction (1
  • mark)
  • ● Tryptase level test – Elevated in mast cell activation/anaphylaxis ((1 mark))
  • ● Eosinophil count (CBC) – Increased eosinophils indicate allergic response ((1 mark))
  • ● IgE-related biochemical estimation (total IgE) – Indicates allergic tendency ((1 mark))
  • ● Mediator release tests (e.g., leukotrienes) – Detect inflammatory mediators in allergy (1
  • mark)
  • B. Immune (immunological) tests ((5 marks))
  • ● Skin prick test (SPT) – Allergen applied to skin; wheal indicates IgE-mediated allergy (1
  • mark)
  • ● Specific IgE test (RAST / ImmunoCAP) – Measures allergen-specific IgE antibodies in
  • blood ((1 mark))
  • ● Elimination diet and oral food challenge – Gold standard for identifying trigger foods (1
  • mark)
  • ● Basophil activation test (BAT) – Measures activation of basophils on exposure to
  • allergens ((1 mark))
  • ● Patch test (for delayed allergy reactions) – Detects non-IgE mediated hypersensitivity (1
  • mark)
questions.final_answer: Option Biochemical tests ((5 marks))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain malaria with causes, symptoms and types of fever.
questions.solution_html:
• Malaria – causes, symptoms and types of fever
  • A. Definition ((1 mark))
  • ● Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and
  • transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito.
  • B. Causes / Etiology ((3 marks))
  • ● Infection by Plasmodium species (e.g., P. vivax, P. falciparum, P. malariae, P. ovale) – 1
  • mark
  • ● Transmission through bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito – (1 mark)
  • ● Parasite multiplies in liver and red blood cells causing fever episodes – (1 mark)
  • C. Symptoms ((3 marks))
  • ● High fever with chills and rigor – (1 mark)
  • ● Headache, body ache, fatigue, and sweating – (1 mark)
  • ● Nausea, vomiting, anemia, and splenomegaly – (1 mark)
  • D. Types of fever pattern in malaria ((3 marks))
  • ● Tertian fever – fever every 48 hours (seen in P. vivax, P. ovale) – (1 mark)
  • ● Quartan fever – fever every 72 hours (seen in P. malariae) – (1 mark)
  • ● Irregular or malignant fever – seen in P. falciparum, often severe and continuous – 1
  • mark.
questions.final_answer: Option Definition ((1 mark))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the dietary management of diarrhoea.
questions.solution_html:
• A. Definition / Aim of diet ((1 mark))
  • ● Dietary management of diarrhoea aims to replace fluids and electrolytes, reduce intestinal
  • irritation, and restore normal bowel function – ((1 mark))
  • B. Fluid and electrolyte replacement ((2 marks))
  • ● Increase intake of oral rehydration solutions (ORS), coconut water, clear soups – (1
  • mark)
  • ● Maintain hydration to prevent dehydration and electrolyte imbalance (sodium, potassium
  • loss) – ((1 mark))
  • C. Energy and protein intake ((2 marks))
  • ● Provide easily digestible, high-energy foods like rice, banana, potatoes – ((1 mark))
  • ● Include moderate protein sources like curd, dal water, eggs (if tolerated) – ((1 mark))
  • D. Foods to include ((2 marks))
  • ● Low-fiber, bland diet (BRAT diet: banana, rice, apple, toast) – ((1 mark))
  • ● Cooked cereals, boiled vegetables, yogurt/probiotics to restore gut flora – ((1 mark))
  • E. Foods to avoid ((2 marks))
  • ● Avoid spicy, fatty, fried foods and caffeine (irritate gut) – ((1 mark))
  • ● Avoid milk (in lactose intolerance), raw vegetables, carbonated drinks – ((1 mark))
  • F. Feeding guidelines / general advice ((1 mark))
  • ● Give small frequent meals, maintain hygiene, and gradually return to normal diet after
  • recovery – ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Option Definition / Aim of diet ((1 mark))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.solution_html:
• A. Definition / Aim of diet ((1 mark))
  • ● Dietary management of diarrhoea aims to replace fluids and electrolytes, reduce intestinal
  • irritation, and restore normal bowel function – ((1 mark))
  • B. Fluid and electrolyte replacement ((2 marks))
  • ● Increase intake of oral rehydration solutions (ORS), coconut water, clear soups – (1
  • mark)
  • ● Maintain hydration to prevent dehydration and electrolyte imbalance (sodium, potassium
  • loss) – ((1 mark))
  • C. Energy and protein intake ((2 marks))
  • ● Provide easily digestible, high-energy foods like rice, banana, potatoes – ((1 mark))
  • ● Include moderate protein sources like curd, dal water, eggs (if tolerated) – ((1 mark))
  • D. Foods to include ((2 marks))
  • ● Low-fiber, bland diet (BRAT diet: banana, rice, apple, toast) – ((1 mark))
  • ● Cooked cereals, boiled vegetables, yogurt/probiotics to restore gut flora – ((1 mark))
  • E. Foods to avoid ((2 marks))
  • ● Avoid spicy, fatty, fried foods and caffeine (irritate gut) – ((1 mark))
  • ● Avoid milk (in lactose intolerance), raw vegetables, carbonated drinks – ((1 mark))
  • F. Feeding guidelines / general advice ((1 mark))
  • ● Give small frequent meals, maintain hygiene, and gradually return to normal diet after
  • recovery – ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Option Definition / Aim of diet ((1 mark))
